title: Regular dodecahedral radiolarian shells cannot arise by crystal-like space partitioning

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Regular dodecahedral radiolarian shells cannot arise by crystal-like space partitioning

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Radiolaria show all five regular polyhedra, including the regular dodecahedron and icosahedron which cannot occur in crystals; therefore the regular radiolarian dodecahedron is not produced by the space-partitioning principles that govern crystallisation.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: If we may safely judge from Haeckel’s figures, the pentagonal dodecahedron of the Radiolarian is perfectly regular, and we must presume, accordingly, that it is not brought about by principles of space-partitioning similar to those which manifest themselves in the phenomenon of crystallisation.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IX, “On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons”; topic “Polyhedral radiolarian skeletons”. Scope: polyhedral Radiolaria (Circoporidae and allies)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch09-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.53

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern geometry can test the critical descriptive premise and periodic crystals indeed constrain rotational symmetry. Available 3D coverage is uncertain, and the broader mechanistic exclusion is less direct than the morphological test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure face, edge and angle equality in 3D polyhedral radiolarian specimens to determine whether regular dodecahedra and icosahedra truly occur. If regularity is confirmed, compare the structure with crystallographic periodic tessellation predictions, while distinguishing crystal lattice formation from broader space-partitioning mechanisms.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Haeckel's drawings may idealize specimen geometry.

Noncrystallographic dodecahedra do not exclude every space-partitioning process.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Once regularity is measured, the crystallographic restriction does the rest of the work, so the empirical task is whether the dodecahedra and icosahedra are actually regular. Images exist, but they are few, often drawings, and not a 3D morphometric series of Circoporidae. A modern subset can test the geometric premise and cannot by itself rule out every non-crystalline space-partitioning process.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure face regularity of radiolarian pentagonal dodecahedra and icosahedra from specimens or scans. Confirmed regularity excludes an origin in crystallographic space-filling; irregular faces, or only those polyhedra that crystals allow, would remove the stated ground for rejecting a crystallization-like partition.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
These skeletons are uncommon, so a regularity measurement will rest on few specimens.

Thompson's premise relies on Haeckel's figures, which may have been regularized.
